name: Christopher Kwok
forbes_bio: Christopher Kwok is the younger son of property mogul Raymond Kwok, chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
He's served as an executive director at Sun Hung Kai since 2016, taking charge of sales, project management and the leasing of major projects.
He's also a member of the Beijing Municipal Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.
In 2012, his father and his uncle Thomas became involved in a bribery investigation. Raymond was acquitted but Thomas was found guilty and sentenced to five years in prison in 2014.
forbes_facts: Christopher's brother, Edward, and three of his cousins are also billionaires.
Christopher and his wife, Rachel Zhao, a former news anchor for China's Phoenix TV, met while they studied at Stanford University in 2013.

name: Nurit Manor
forbes_bio: Nurit Manor is a controlling shareholder of Harel Insurance, an Israeli insurance and financial services company.
She is one of three siblings - alongside Gideon and Yair Hamburger - who control Harel through G.Y.N Consulting, the family's privately held company.
Harel, now one of Israel's biggest institutional financial firms, was founded in 1939 and has remained under family control.
Harel manages assets valued at NIS 571 billion ($176 billion) and operates across health, motor, life insurance, pensions and asset management.

name: Larry Culp
forbes_bio: Larry Culp is chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace (formerly known as General Electric).

He took over GE in 2018 and has broken up the bloated conglomerate into three separate public companies after spinning off its healthcare business as GE HealthCare in 2023 and its energy business as GE Vernova in 2024.
Culp also serves as chairman of GE Healthcare.
Culp started his career at Danaher, the industrial conglomerate founded by billionaire brothers Mitchell and Steven Rales.
He joined Danaher in 1990 and served as president and CEO from 2001 to 2015.

name: Raymond Kwok
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Raymond Kwok is the youngest son of the late Kwok Tak-seng, cofounder of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
Since 2011 he's served first as the developer's cochairman and now as the chairman.
The three Kwok brothers inherited the publicly traded company after the death of their father in 1990.
The brothers fought for a decade over the family's assets until Walter (d. 2018), the eldest brother, decided to drop his lawsuit.
Raymond's son Edward has been an alternate director and his other son, Christopher, has been an executive director. Both are also billionaires.
forbes_facts: Both he and his brother Thomas are devout Christians. They built an evangelical theme park, Noah's Ark, on Ma Wan Island in Hong Kong.

name: Justin Yuan
forbes_bio: Justin Yuan is CEO of Moonton Games, best known for "Mobile Legends: Bang Bang."
China's ByteDance bought Moonton for approximately $4 billion in 2021.
Moonton is headquartered in Shanghai.

name: Tsai Cheng-Chiu
sec_insider_companies: ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (ASX) - Chairman & President, SPIL
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2018); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Tsai Cheng-chiu is a director of Cathay Financial Holdings, a leading financial services company in Taiwan.
The company made his father, Tsai Wan-lin, Taiwan's wealthiest man before he died in 2004.
Half-brothers Cheng-ta and Hong-tu are billionaires, as are their cousins Richard and Daniel Tsai.

name: Lim Wee Chai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Lim Wee Chai started Top Glove with his wife Tong Siew Bee in 1991 and took the company public in 2001.
Top Glove is one of the world's largest producers of rubber gloves. It has 51 factories with an annual capacity of 95 billion gloves.
Lim, whose parents are rubber plantation owners and traders, also holds a stake in property developer Tropicana.
In March 2022, Lim postponed plans for a Hong Kong listing amid a sharp drop in profits.
